message.content:
{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study reports a quantitative measure of agreement (concordance rate) between animal toxicity studies and human clinical toxicity outcomes for pharmaceuticals. It analyzes data from 150 compounds and 221 human toxicity events, calculating a true positive concordance rate of 71% for rodent and nonrodent species.",
  "arm": "toxicology",
  "arm_evidence": "The main aim of this project was to examine the strengths and weaknesses of animal studies to predict human toxicity (HT).",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The database was developed from a survey which covered only those compounds where HTs were identified during clinical development of new pharmaceuticals, determining whether animal toxicity studies identified concordant target organ toxicities in humans.",
  "model_type": "regulatory-dataset",
  "model_evidence": "This report summarizes the results of a multinational pharmaceutical company survey and the outcome of an International Life Sciences Institute (ILSI) Workshop (April 1999)... The database was developed from a survey which covered only those compounds where HTs were identified during clinical development of new pharmaceuticals...",
  "species": [
    "mouse",
    "rat",
    "non-human-primate",
    "dog"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The results showed the true positive HT concordance rate of 71% for rodent and nonrodent species, with nonrodents alone being predictive for 63% of HTs and rodents alone for 43%.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "Data collected included codified compounds, therapeutic category, the HT organ system affected, and the species and duration of studies in which the corresponding HT was either first identified or not observed."
}
